[0] everyday_reading (E): Folk meaning: in English, 'while the dog is in the city, keep walking' is monitored continuously, so the walk stops the instant it leaves. Java rule: the while condition is tested only before each pass, so the guard must make every index used in the body legal at that moment.
[1] misconception (M) -> LoopVariableNotUpdated: wrong rule: A while loop ends by itself even if nothing in the body changes the variable tested in the condition. Right rule: If no statement in the body changes a variable in the condition, a condition that was true stays true and the loop never ends.
[2] inconsistent_trace (T) -> LoopVariableNotUpdated: Points to LT: the guard is tested before every pass, and the body runs only if it is true. Inconsistent application: the trace applies the bounds test only at the first pass, or after the body has already used the out-of-range index. (here mixing in: "A while loop ends by itself even if nothing in the body changes the variable tested in the condition")
[3] misconception (M) -> BodyChangeIgnoredByCondition: wrong rule: Changing the loop variable inside the body does not affect the loop condition; the loop still runs its planned number of times. Right rule: The condition is tested with the current value of the variable, including changes made in the body.
[4] misconception (M) -> LoopCountByIntent: wrong rule: How many times a loop runs is decided by what the program is meant to do, so it may go on after its condition is false. Right rule: The loop runs only while its condition is true when tested; it stops at the first false test.
[5] misconception (M) -> LoopConditionValidatedLater: wrong rule: If a loop condition is false at first but would become true later, the loop still runs. Right rule: A while loop whose condition is false at the first test runs zero times; nothing later revives it.
[6] misconception (M) -> LessGreaterSwapped: wrong rule: < and > mean the same thing (or a < b means a is greater than b). Right rule: a < b is true when a is smaller than b; a > b when a is larger.

[0] names_the_element (N): Identity: a loop guard is a loop-continuation test that also guards the body against an illegal statement, typically an out-of-bounds array access.
[1] states_the_rule (S): Declarative: code the loop exit test so that whenever the body runs, all indices it uses are legal, e.g. while (x > 0 && x < N-1 && y > 0 && y < N-1) before reading a[x-1][y], a[x+1][y], ...

[0] line_by_line_trace (LT): Sequencing: before each pass the guard is evaluated left to right, and && stops at the first false operand; the body runs only if the whole guard is true; after the body the guard is tested again with the updated values.
[1] output_prediction (OP): Result: the loop ends normally, with no exception, when an index reaches the boundary; in SelfAvoidingWalk that means the dog has escaped.
[2] one_step_execution (OS): State transition: one guard evaluation changes no variable; it either admits one more pass with legal indices or ends the loop.

[0] relation_to_neighbour (R): Because an out-of-bounds index stops the program, the guard tests the bounds before the body uses the index, and it must cover every neighbour index (x-1, x+1) the body reads.
[1] purpose_of_the_whole (P): Plan/role: the guard-before-use plan. A single test both terminates the loop (event: reached the edge) and protects every array access in the body.

[0] predict_a_change (C) -> LoopVariableNotUpdated: Conservation: inside the body the guard's invariant holds (0 < x < N-1, so x-1 and x+1 are legal indices). Weakening the guard (x >= 0) or putting the array test before the bounds test in && breaks it.
[1] transfer_to_a_new_program (X): Applicability: use a guarded while loop when iteration continues until a data-dependent event and the body indexes an array with a moving position (walks, searches). For a full traversal, a for loop with i < a.length is the simpler guard.
[2] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The guard must make every index in the body legal. Kind: run-time exception. Trigger class: the guard is missing, too weak (x >= 0 && x < N while the body reads a[x+1]), or ordered wrongly (a[i] != 0 && i < n) so the access happens before the bounds test (ArrayIndexOutOfBoundsException)
[3] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The body must change a variable in the guard. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: no statement in the body updates the guarded index, so the loop never ends (infinite loop)
[4] diagnose_an_error (D): rule broken: The relational operators must express the intended bound. Kind: silent logic error. Trigger class: < and > (or < and <=) are swapped, so the loop runs zero times or one pass too many
